questions.q: In a cloud environment, what kinds of traffic does TLS actually secure?
options: Traffic between a client and a cloud service, and traffic between cloud services talking to each other behind the scenes
Only traffic that crosses the public internet, never traffic between two services inside the same cloud
Only traffic sent from a mobile app, never traffic from a browser
TLS only secures data at rest, not data in motion
questions.explain: TLS covers any network hop — client-to-service or service-to-service — whether it crosses the public internet or stays inside the provider's own network.

questions.q: What does Azure's "Secure transfer required" setting actually do?
options: It rejects any plain HTTP request to a storage account, enforcing HTTPS-only access, and is enabled by default on new accounts
It encrypts data at rest using a customer-managed key
It is an optional, rarely-used setting that must be manually enabled on every account
It only applies to Amazon S3, not Azure Storage Accounts
questions.explain: Secure transfer required rejects plain HTTP outright and is on by default for new Azure Storage Accounts.

questions.q: How can Amazon S3 enforce HTTPS-only access to a bucket?
options: With a bucket policy that denies any request where aws:SecureTransport is false
S3 has no way to enforce HTTPS-only access at all
By disabling the bucket's public DNS name
By requiring a customer-managed key for every request
questions.explain: A bucket policy checking the aws:SecureTransport condition key is the real mechanism S3 offers for enforcing encrypted-only access.

questions.q: Why do Azure and AWS now enforce a minimum TLS version, such as TLS 1.2, across most managed services?
options: Older TLS versions like 1.0 and 1.1 have known weaknesses, so connections that try to negotiate them are refused rather than silently downgraded
Older TLS versions are actually faster and only disabled for cost reasons
Minimum TLS version enforcement is unrelated to security and only affects billing
TLS version has no bearing on the handshake or session key exchange
questions.explain: Enforcing a minimum TLS version prevents a connection from silently downgrading to an outdated, insecure version of TLS.

questions.q: In the cloud, where does the TLS certificate that proves a service's identity typically come from?
options: Services like Azure Key Vault or AWS Certificate Manager, which issue and can automatically renew certificates
Each individual application developer must generate a brand-new certificate authority from scratch
TLS certificates are not used in cloud environments at all
Certificates are only needed for client-to-service traffic, never service-to-service traffic
questions.explain: Key Vault and AWS Certificate Manager centralize certificate issuance and renewal, preventing certificates from silently expiring.
